DIRECTION IS NEAR-OPTIMAL: given today, it calls tomorrow higher or lower correctly 70.9% of the time against a simulated ceiling of 74.1% -- 96% of what is achievable. Naive manages 34.2%.
LEVEL HAS ROOM: within-ticker R-squared(log) is 0.247 against a ceiling of 0.533, so 46% captured. The ceiling is measured, not assumed: a Kalman fit puts Var(latent log-vol) at 0.125 against Var(measurement noise) 0.110, so 92% of the day-to-day movement in the observed series is estimation error that nothing can forecast.
It beats the stock's own trailing 60-day average on 50 of 50 tickers, and naive on QLIKE 0.3517 against 0.5271.
NOT BETTER THAN PLAIN HAR ON QLIKE. A HAR fitted on each stock's own history, in levels, scores QLIKE 0.3354 against this ensemble's 0.3530 (volatility_roster_garman_klass.json, volatility_tracking.json), and 0.334 against 0.347 for a three-member version on identical rows (out_of_panel.json). The ensemble was trained for TRACKING, squared error in logs, and wins there: direction 71.0% against HAR's 68.0%, within-stock R2 0.244 against 0.216. QLIKE punishes under-forecasting, and a level model trained on squared error sits higher. Which is better depends on the loss; neither dominates.
BEATEN ALONG THE WAY on the tracking objective: GARCH, GJR-GARCH, CARR, a cubic spline that provably nests HAR, a pooled LSTM and BiLSTM, Chronos-Bolt zero-shot, a Kalman state-space model, wavelet decomposition and temporal-hierarchy reconciliation. Most of the gain came from training in log space rather than from any architecture.
CAVEAT: the pooled R-squared of 0.452 is flattered by the easy cross-sectional half -- 0.935 between tickers, 0.247 within one.
AND THE CROSS-SECTION IS MOSTLY PERSISTENCE: ranking stocks by this forecast gives a daily Spearman of 0.631 against what then happens, but ranking by a plain trailing 66-day average gives 0.610. The model adds +0.021 (t = 12.3), real and small.
INTERVAL: the 80% band covered 80.6% and the 95% band 94.8% of held-out days. One width is shared by every stock, so per-stock coverage of the 80% band runs from 72.4% to 86.1%.

figures.label: Forecast volatility, next session (annualised)
figures.evidence: QLIKE 0.3517 on 61,303 walk-forward forecasts; beats each stock's own trailing average on 50 of 50 tickers. LIMIT: within one stock the forecast explains R-squared 0.247 of the day-to-day level against an attainable 0.533 (46%), so read it as a rough level, not a precise one (re-measured: 0.247).

figures.label: 80% interval
figures.evidence: held-out coverage 80.6% against a nominal 80% on 61,303 walk-forward forecasts across all stocks (range across stocks 72.4% to 86.1%). On this stock it covered 82.0%. Misses are lopsided: realised volatility lands ABOVE the band on 10.4% of days and below it on 8.9%, so the upper edge is the weaker one.

figures.label: 95% interval
figures.evidence: held-out coverage 94.8% against a nominal 95% on 61,303 walk-forward forecasts across all stocks (range across stocks 90.5% to 97.4%). On this stock it covered 94.2%. Misses are lopsided: realised volatility lands ABOVE the band on 3.4% of days and below it on 1.8%, so the upper edge is the weaker one.

figures.label: Tomorrow against today
figures.evidence: calls higher-or-lower correctly 70.9% of the time against a measured ceiling of 74.1%, so 29% of these calls are wrong and at most 3.2% of that is recoverable by any model (re-measured: 70.9%).

figures.label: Realised volatility, latest session (annualised)
figures.evidence: Garman-Klass estimate from one day's open, high, low and close. A noisy measurement: about half of its day-to-day variance is estimation error.

limits: This is how BIG the move will be, never which way the price goes.
One session ahead only. Nothing here speaks to next week.

registry_skill.note:
Measured on 42,834 held-out stock-days across 45 names, the 80% band covered 79.4% and the 95% band 94.8%.
EFFECTIVELY TIED WITH A PER-STOCK HAR. Seven width sources, one causal calibration recipe: Winkler score 6.514 against 6.534 for a HAR fitted on each stock (Diebold-Mariano p=0.003) at 80%, and 10.229 against 10.265 (p=0.11, not significant) at 95%. Best of the seven on 34 of 45 stocks at 80% and 27 of 45 at 95%. Clearly narrower than constant, trailing 60-day, EWMA, GARCH or carried-forward volatility (6.704 and 10.810 for the best of those). An earlier comparison omitted HAR and reported a 3-5% gain; against HAR the gain is 0.3%.
NO DIRECTIONAL SKILL, by measurement: forecast volatility correlates +0.018 with the next return, and the share of up days is 50.2% when it is high and 50.1% when it is low. The point is today's close.
WEAK ON WILD DAYS: the 80% band covers 92% of the calmest third of days and 65% of the most volatile third. Average coverage hides that.

figures.label: Best single guess for the next close
figures.evidence: this is today's close. The volatility forecast says nothing about direction: its correlation with the next return is +0.018, and the share of up days is 50.2% when it is high against 50.1% when it is low. No price model in this project beats today's close as a point forecast.

figures.label: 80% range for the next close
figures.evidence: held-out coverage 79.4% against a nominal 80% on 42,834 stock-days. Interval score 6.514 against 6.534 for the best of six other volatility sources, a per-stock HAR -- effectively a tie with that simple model, and clearly narrower than constant, trailing, EWMA or GARCH volatility. LIMIT: on the most volatile third of days it covers only 65%.

figures.evidence: the line above, restated as a percentage

figures.evidence: held-out coverage 94.8% against a nominal 95% on 42,834 stock-days. LIMIT: on the most volatile third of days it covers only 88%.

registry_skill.note:
MEASURED ON THE EQUAL-WEIGHTED MARKET PROXY, NOT ON A STOCK. There the regime-conditional VaR passes both coverage tests and the unconditional version is REJECTED (Kupiec p=0.0057 at 95%, p=0.0004 at 99%).
THE PASS IS ROBUST; THE P-VALUE IS NOT A STABLE NUMBER. On the panel as cached to 2026-09-21 the same code gave Kupiec p=0.273 and Christoffersen p=0.237. Nine more sessions, and the removal of four flat rows the vendor had served for exchange holidays, moved them to 0.831 and 0.575. Across ten random starts of the HMM on the served regime, both tests pass every time, with Kupiec p between 0.63 and 0.96 and Christoffersen between 0.22 and 0.58. Quote the verdict, not the third decimal.
THE PASS DOES NOT TRANSFER TO SINGLE STOCKS. Re-run per stock on the 50-name panel, the regime-conditional VaR passes both tests on 12 of 46 testable names (15 on the 2026-09-21 panel; 4 have too little history). Of the 22 Kupiec rejections, 18 overstate the loss and 4 understate it. Conditioning still helps: unconditional passes on 6 of 46.
Expected shortfall and the multi-day Markov VaR are not backtested at all. agents/risk_composition.py attaches each stock's own backtest to its VaR for this reason.

figures.evidence: walk-forward on this stock, 1167 days: breached on 3.7% of them against a 5% target. Christoffersen p=0.084 passes. Kupiec p=0.0309 REJECTS coverage: too few breaches -- this VaR overstates the loss, so it errs on the safe side.

registry_skill.note:

DIRECTION IS NEAR-OPTIMAL: given today, it calls tomorrow higher or lower correctly 70.9% of the time against a simulated ceiling of 74.1% -- 96% of what is achievable. Naive manages 34.2%.
LEVEL HAS ROOM: within-ticker R-squared(log) is 0.247 against a ceiling of 0.533, so 46% captured. The ceiling is measured, not assumed: a Kalman fit puts Var(latent log-vol) at 0.125 against Var(measurement noise) 0.110, so 92% of the day-to-day movement in the observed series is estimation error that nothing can forecast.
It beats the stock's own trailing 60-day average on 50 of 50 tickers, and naive on QLIKE 0.3517 against 0.5271.

registry_skill.note:
Measured on 61,303 strictly causal walk-forward forecasts.
DIRECTION IS NEAR-OPTIMAL: given today, it calls tomorrow higher or lower correctly 70.9% of the time against a simulated ceiling of 74.1% -- 96% of what is achievable. Naive manages 34.2%.
LEVEL HAS ROOM: within-ticker R-squared(log) is 0.247 against a ceiling of 0.533, so 46% captured. The ceiling is measured, not assumed: a Kalman fit puts Var(latent log-vol) at 0.125 against Var(measurement noise) 0.110, so 92% of the day-to-day movement in the observed series is estimation error that nothing can forecast.
It beats the stock's own trailing 60-day average on 50 of 50 tickers, and naive on QLIKE 0.3517 against 0.5271.
NOT BETTER THAN PLAIN HAR ON QLIKE. A HAR fitted on each stock's own history, in levels, scores QLIKE 0.3354 against this ensemble's 0.3530 (volatility_roster_garman_klass.json, volatility_tracking.json), and 0.334 against 0.347 for a three-member version on identical rows (out_of_panel.json). The ensemble was trained for TRACKING, squared error in logs, and wins there: direction 71.0% against HAR's 68.0%, within-stock R2 0.244 against 0.216. QLIKE punishes under-forecasting, and a level model trained on squared error sits higher. Which is better depends on the loss; neither dominates.
BEATEN ALONG THE WAY on the tracking objective: GARCH, GJR-GARCH, CARR, a cubic spline that provably nests HAR, a pooled LSTM and BiLSTM, Chronos-Bolt zero-shot, a Kalman state-space model, wavelet decomposition and temporal-hierarchy reconciliation. Most of the gain came from training in log space rather than from any architecture.
CAVEAT: the pooled R-squared of 0.452 is flattered by the easy cross-sectional half -- 0.935 between tickers, 0.247 within one.
AND THE CROSS-SECTION IS MOSTLY PERSISTENCE: ranking stocks by this forecast gives a daily Spearman of 0.631 against what then happens, but ranking by a plain trailing 66-day average gives 0.610. The model adds +0.021 (t = 12.3), real and small.
INTERVAL: the 80% band covered 80.6% and the 95% band 94.8% of held-out days. One width is shared by every stock, so per-stock coverage of the 80% band runs from 72.4% to 86.1%.

registry_skill.note:
Measured on 61,303 strictly causal walk-forward forecasts.
DIRECTION IS NEAR-OPTIMAL: given today, it calls tomorrow higher or lower correctly 70.9% of the time against a simulated ceiling of 74.1% -- 96% of what is achievable. Naive manages 34.2%.
LEVEL HAS ROOM: within-ticker R-squared(log) is 0.247 against a ceiling of 0.533, so 46% captured. The ceiling is measured, not assumed: a Kalman fit puts Var(latent log-vol) at 0.125 against Var(measurement noise) 0.110, so 92% of the day-to-day movement in the observed series is estimation error that nothing can forecast.
It beats the stock's own trailing 60-day average on 50 of 50 tickers, and naive on QLIKE 0.3517 against 0.5271.
NOT BETTER THAN PLAIN HAR ON QLIKE. A HAR fitted on each stock's own history, in levels, scores QLIKE 0.3354 against this ensemble's 0.3530 (volatility_roster_garman_klass.json, volatility_tracking.json), and 0.334 against 0.347 for a three-member version on identical rows (out_of_panel.json). registry_skill.note:
Measured on 61,303 strictly causal walk-forward forecasts.
DIRECTION IS NEAR-OPTIMAL: given today, it calls tomorrow higher or lower correctly 70.9% of the time against a simulated ceiling of 74.1% -- 96% of what is achievable. Naive manages 34.2%.
LEVEL HAS ROOM: within-ticker R-squared(log) is 0.247 against a ceiling of 0.533, so 46% captured. The ceiling is measured, not assumed: a Kalman fit puts Var(latent log-vol) at 0.125 against Var(measurement noise) 0.110, so 92% of the day-to-day movement in the observed series is estimation error that nothing can forecast.
It beats the stock's own trailing 60-day average on 50 of 50 tickers, and naive on QLIKE 0.3517 against 0.5271.
NOT BETTER THAN PLAIN HAR ON QLIKE. A HAR fitted on each stock's own history, in levels, scores QLIKE 0.3354 against this ensemble's 0.3530 (volatility_roster_garman_klass.json, volatility_tracking.json), and 0.334 against 0.347 for a three-member version on identical rows (out_of_panel.json). The ensemble was trained for TRACKING, squared error in logs, and wins there: direction 71.0% against HAR's 68.0%, within-stock R2 0.244 against 0.216. QLIKE punishes under-forecasting, and a level model trained on squared error sits higher. Which is better depends on the loss; neither dominates.
BEATEN ALONG THE WAY on the tracking objective: GARCH, GJR-GARCH, CARR, a cubic spline that provably nests HAR, a pooled LSTM and BiLSTM, Chronos-Bolt zero-shot, a Kalman state-space model, wavelet decomposition and temporal-hierarchy reconciliation. Most of the gain came from training in log space rather than from any architecture.
CAVEAT: the pooled R-squared of 0.452 is flattered by the easy cross-sectional half -- 0.935 between tickers, 0.247 within one.
AND THE CROSS-SECTION IS MOSTLY PERSISTENCE: ranking stocks by this forecast gives a daily Spearman of 0.631 against what then happens, but ranking by a plain trailing 66-day average gives 0.610. The model adds +0.021 (t = 12.3), real and small.
INTERVAL: the 80% band covered 80.6% and the 95% band 94.8% of held-out days. One width is shared by every stock, so per-stock coverage of the 80% band runs from 72.4% to 86.1%.
